status: draft for owner review; hex values are design targets, not measured from a reference

palette.rule: Braj daylight earth tones first. Colour comes from the scene's light source, never from a constant glow or neon edge.

miasma.rule: muted, low-saturation fume layers only; no glowing neon vapour

divine_light.rule: Warm gold only where a scene light falls on a gold garment or the river surface (sun, dawn). Never a halo by default. Purification may use one clear sunlit gold bloom, once per episode at most.

palette.skin_range: Indian complexions varied by character (see characters). No lightened skin on any character; Krishna is cloud-dark indigo-grey.

line.colour: warm dark brown-black #1E1A17 on skin and cloth; deep indigo #1B2538 on Krishna and Kaliya bodies; never pure #000000
line.rule: variable weight: thicker on the silhouette and under the chin, thinner in folds; no outline on background plates

shading.tones: 2 cel tones plus one hard core-shadow plane; the shade is 20-30 percent darker than the base, hue-shifted toward the ground colour
shading.reflected_bounce: warm ground bounce on the underside of arms and cloth (sand or grass colour), never cool blue bounce on skin
shading.rule: no gradient airbrush on figures; gradients allowed only in painted backgrounds

rim_light.allowed_when: a visible low sun or a bright water surface sits behind or beside the figure in that shot
rim_light.colour: matches the motivating light (gold at dawn, pale sky-blue over water, never neon)
rim_light.limit: at most one rim-lit figure per shot; never on faces during dialogue or acting beats
rim_light.forbidden: constant rim on every character, neon edge, rim that has no source in the frame

rules: Identity: Krishna is a child of about 7-8, wearing a golden pitambara and the black Kali Kamli, with the Srivatsa mark on the chest (ŚB 10.16.9 lists the golden pitambara and the Srivatsa mark).
Symbols are used only when the scene names them. The peacock feather and flute are attributes; a full divine crown is reserved for divine-vision frames.
Krishna's feet and the lotus-foot footprint are shown only where the source names them (ŚB 10.16.35-37, footprint seal on the hoods after the purification).
Garuda's Amrit Kalash and the golden drops are a KATHAVACHAK_VARIATION: shown in the flashback only, flagged in the edit notes.
restrictions: No invented supernatural effects: no lightning beams, no energy aura, no magic circles
No glowing neon venom; poison is dark fume and dead colour
No exact counts of hoods, gopis or serpents shown as a crowd of many; give a visible number and suggest the rest by depth and shadow
Kaliya is a serpent, never a dragon or humanoid monster

composition_grammar.source_painting_traits: high or aerial horizon, flat colour fields, several narrative moments in one frame, layered planes, figures set in a rhythmic stance (tribhanga for Krishna), ornamented borders
composition_grammar.translation_to_2_5d: fg = blurred foreground foliage or sand (depth cue); mid = the cel-shaded acting layer; bg = flat painted bands with aerial haze; keep the horizon high on water scenes and place the tribhanga pose against a flat band of colour
